main_text.p: minum speciem quidem referat, sed tamen quoad succum contaminet, ita ut in corruptissimos fructus exe-ant. Proin vitis Sodomæ in agris Gomorrhæ excrescens alludit ad pessimas illas frutices, quæ in istis oris notan-tur, de quibus multa veteres. Tertullianus in apologetico cap. 40, de hac regione loquens, dicit. Olet adhuc incendio terra, & si qua illic arborum poma colantur, oculis tenus, caterum contacta cinerescunt. Augustinus de civitate Dei libr. 21. cap. 8. Prodigiosa fuligine horrori est, & poma ejus interiorem favillam mendaci superficie maturitatis includunt. Isidorus Etym. libr. 14. c. 3. Nascuntur ibi poma viventia, sub tanta specie maturitatis, ut edendi desiderium gignant: si carpas, satisfacunt[?] ac resolvuntur in cineres, fumumque exhalant, quasi adhuc ardeant. Eadem tradunt Ambrosius libr. 1. de Abrah. cap. 6. Clem. Alex. libr. 2. Pædag. cap. 10. Hæc jam ante memoriæ prodiderat Philo Judæus libr. de Abrahamo, ac præ primis Josephus de Bello Jud. libr. 5. cap. 5. Colore quidem & specie, inquit, aliorum fructuum sunt persimiles, tactu vero in carpentium manibus resolvuntur in fumum ac cineres. Vites itaque Sodomæ in agris Gomorrhæ egregium præstant Symbolum ecclesiæ fucatæ, per hypocrisin veram mentiens ecclesiam, videturque quam proximè referre populum Judaicum carnalem, qui olim istas mundi oras incoluit: hic vero quantocius concipiuntur ab eo separati genuini Abrahami filii, populi pars ele-cta, in sacris tantummodo pro Sodomâ reputatur, & pro Gomorrhâ. Cons. Deut. 29: 23. Jes. 1:4. 10: 23. Jerem 24: 14. Zeph. 2:9. Hic loci notandum, quod non ipsa vitis Sodomæ in agris Gomorrhæ exhibeatur, sed ejus propago ex vite Sodomæ sumpta & ex agris Gomorrhæ in aliam oram translata: atque sic

page.notes: Printed words are copied as seen. Doubtful readings: "satisfacunt" (first letters of the word unclear, marked [?]); "gignant:" (the mark after the word may be a semicolon); "caterum" and "viventia" are read from a slightly blurred scan. Long s is written as s throughout, so "Conf." is given as "Cons." and "Jef." as "Jes.". Printed hyphens at line ends are kept (exe-ant, notan-tur, ele-cta). The italic and roman split for author names (Tertullianus, Augustinus, Isidorus, Ambrosius, Philo, Josephus) follows the scan and is uncertain. The scan is of the page's right half and the left margin is cropped, so the first line may begin on a word fragment carried over from the previous page.
